SMTO-JOB-0013 — The Gateway turned down a background job request

GUID: c8a622df-c318-4021-b05b-ee1620365ae4
Slug: invalid-job-request
Domain: JOB · Subsystem: job

What happened

  • SMTO asked the Gateway (the helper program that runs commands on a computer) to start, read or stop a background job, but the request was incomplete. A refused start did not run; for other requests, the job's status is unknown.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the agent continue; it usually fixes the request on its own, for example by using the job reference the Gateway gave it. This usually comes from a small mistake in the agent's request, not a problem on your computer.
  2. If you asked about a particular job, tell the agent which one you mean, for example "the backup job you started earlier", instead of typing a job reference. A typed or old reference may not match any job the Gateway knows.
  3. Before asking for the work to start again, check whether it already happened, for example whether the expected file or change is there. If the job was already running, a failed status or stop request doesn't mean it ended.

What success looks like

  • The task shows the job's status or output, or a new job starts and shows as running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't start the same command again until you're sure the first one didn't already run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway rejected a job request because its action, job_id (1–100 of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _ or -), start command or target, log range (offset ≥ 0, limit 1–12000) or exec-cancel execution_id was missing or invalid.

What this means

  • A new job request fails its action/payload/identity contract, a job ID fails its bounded syntax, log offset/limit is invalid or execution cancellation lacks execution_id. Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.

Why this can happen

  • A new job request fails its action/payload/identity contract, a job ID fails its bounded syntax, log offset/limit is invalid or execution cancellation lacks execution_id.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific action, observed identity and log range; invalid control lookup must not be treated as a failed job.

How to fix it

  • Read the request details in the Server log or Technical details: start needs a non-empty command, a valid target and a valid job_id; logs needs offset ≥ 0 and 1 ≤ limit ≤ 12000; exec cancel needs execution_id. Use the job_id the Gateway returned rather than constructing one or reusing an unrelated job's ID.
  • Use the advertised job action and a valid observed job identity. A rejected new launch is not permission to reuse an unrelated job identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported scoped action validates with an exact owned identity and bounded payload.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
